questions.stem: About the autonomic nervous system:
options: Its activity is predominantly voluntary
It regulates cardiac muscle, smooth muscle and glands
Its control centres lie in the CNS
"Autonomic" means independent of the brain
questions.explanation: The ANS is predominantly involuntary but not independent of the brain: autonomic = automatic, not autonomous. Its centres lie in the CNS.

questions.stem: Somatic versus autonomic motor systems:
options: The somatic transmitter is ACh acting on nicotinic muscle (Nm) receptors
The somatic pathway uses one neuron from the CNS to the muscle
The autonomic pathway usually uses two neurons relayed in a peripheral ganglion
The effect of the somatic system on its target is excitatory or inhibitory
questions.explanation: Somatic effects are always excitatory; autonomic effects can be excitatory or inhibitory, through ACh or NE depending on the pathway.

questions.stem: About the components of the ANS:
options: The parasympathetic division has a craniosacral origin and supports "rest and digest"
The enteric nervous system is an intrinsic gut network that can work on its own and is modulated by both divisions
The sympathetic division has a thoracolumbar origin and mobilizes the body for "fight or flight"
Sympathetic preganglionic neurons lie in the lateral horn of the spinal cord from T1 to L2
questions.explanation: Sympathetic preganglionic neurons lie in the lateral horn of the spinal cord from T1 to L2.

questions.stem: Which sympathetic ganglion — target pairs are correct?
options: Sympathetic chain (paravertebral) — heart, lungs, sweat glands and blood vessels
Coeliac ganglion — stomach, liver, pancreas, spleen
Superior mesenteric ganglion — eye and salivary glands
Inferior mesenteric ganglion — distal colon, rectum, pelvic organs
questions.explanation: The eye and salivary glands are supplied through the sympathetic chain; the superior mesenteric ganglion supplies the small intestine and proximal colon.

questions.stem: The adrenal medulla:
options: Releases about 80 % noradrenaline and 20 % adrenaline
Has chromaffin cells stimulated by preganglionic ACh through Nn receptors
Receives a postganglionic sympathetic fibre
Behaves like a modified sympathetic ganglion
questions.explanation: The preganglionic fibre reaches the adrenal medulla directly (no postganglionic neuron); it releases adrenaline (~80 %) and noradrenaline (~20 %) into the blood.

questions.stem: About the parasympathetic outflow:
options: The vagus nerve carries most parasympathetic outflow
The otic ganglion supplies the submandibular gland
It arises from cranial nerves III, VII, IX, X and the sacral cord S2–S4
The ciliary ganglion supplies the lacrimal glands
questions.explanation: Ciliary ganglion → eye; pterygopalatine → lacrimal and nasal glands; submandibular ganglion → submandibular and sublingual glands; otic ganglion → parotid.

questions.stem: Comparing the two divisions:
options: Parasympathetic: ganglia near or within the target organs
Sympathetic: usually short preganglionic and long postganglionic fibres
Parasympathetic: high divergence with widespread effects
Sympathetic: ganglia within the target organs
questions.explanation: Sympathetic ganglia lie near the vertebral column or abdominal arteries, with high divergence (widespread effects). Parasympathetic ganglia lie near/in organs: long pre, short post, localized effects.

questions.stem: About transmission in the autonomic ganglia:
options: The preganglionic neuron releases ACh in both divisions
Sympathetic ganglia use NE acting on α receptors
The Nn receptor is a fast ligand-gated cation channel with no second messenger
ACh acts on neuronal nicotinic (Nn) receptors
questions.explanation: Rule 1: every autonomic ganglion, sympathetic or parasympathetic, uses ACh on Nn receptors (fast ligand-gated channels).

questions.stem: At the target organ:
options: Sympathetic postganglionic fibres always release NE, without exception
Parasympathetic fibres act on nicotinic muscle (Nm) receptors
Most sympathetic postganglionic fibres release NE onto α or β receptors
Parasympathetic postganglionic fibres release ACh onto muscarinic receptors
questions.explanation: Rule 2: parasympathetic ACh → M; most sympathetic NE → α/β. Eccrine sweat glands are the exception: sympathetic but cholinergic.

questions.stem: A patient taking a drug that blocks M₃ receptors notices that they sweat less. Which statements explain this?
options: Sweat glands receive parasympathetic innervation
Sweat glands respond to NE acting on α₁ receptors
Eccrine sweat glands receive sympathetic cholinergic fibres
Sympathetic postganglionic fibres to sweat glands release ACh onto M₃ receptors
questions.explanation: Sweating is the key cholinergic exception of the sympathetic system (ACh → M₃). Sweat glands have no parasympathetic innervation.

questions.stem: About the special cases of sympathetic transmission:
options: Adipose tissue uses NE normally, through β₃ receptors, for lipolysis
Eccrine sweat glands are the key cholinergic exception
The kidney uses NE normally, through β₁ receptors, to release renin
Bronchi depend mainly on circulating adrenaline acting on β₂ receptors
questions.explanation: Kidney (β₁) and adipose tissue (β₃) are not exceptions, just particular subtypes. The cholinergic exception is the eccrine sweat gland.

questions.stem: Which receptor — signalling pairs are correct?
options: β₁, β₂, β₃ — mainly Gs → ↑ cAMP
M₂ — Gi/o, ↓ cAMP, and opening of K⁺ channels in the heart
α₂ — Gs → ↑ cAMP
α₁ — Gi/o → ↓ cAMP
questions.explanation: α₁ is coupled to Gq (IP₃/DAG → ↑ Ca²⁺); α₂ and M₂/M₄ to Gi/o. Memory aid: Gs = Stimulates cAMP, Gi = Inhibits cAMP, Gq = Ca²⁺.

questions.stem: Where are these receptors mainly located?
options: β₁ — heart and kidney
β₃ — adipose tissue and detrusor
α₂ — presynaptic terminals, where they increase NE release
M₃ — smooth muscle of the gut, bronchi, bladder and iris, and glands
questions.explanation: Presynaptic α₂ receptors reduce NE release (negative feedback); α₂ is also found on pancreatic β-cells.

questions.stem: The same receptor can have different effects depending on the tissue:
options: Endothelial M₃ contracts the vessels directly
M₃ contracts the iris sphincter
Endothelial M₃ relaxes vascular smooth muscle by releasing nitric oxide
The organ response depends on the transmitter, the receptor subtype and the tissue
questions.explanation: Endothelial M₃ acts indirectly: it releases NO, which relaxes the smooth muscle of the vessel wall.

questions.stem: About visceral reflexes:
options: A short reflex is integrated in the enteric plexus or an autonomic ganglion without passing through the CNS
Urination is an example of a long reflex
A long reflex passes through the spinal cord or brainstem
A short reflex coordinates several organs
questions.explanation: Short reflexes are fast and local (small part of one organ, e.g. gut wall stretch); long reflexes go through the CNS and can coordinate several organs (bladder emptying).

questions.stem: During an exam, a student's heart speeds up and digestion slows. About the central control of the ANS:
options: The cortex and limbic system adapt autonomic responses to emotions
The brainstem is the centre of the bladder and bowel emptying reflexes
The ANS has no central control: it is autonomous
The hypothalamus is the main coordinator of autonomic responses and homeostasis
questions.explanation: The ANS is controlled by a hierarchy: cortex/limbic system → hypothalamus → brainstem → spinal cord. Bladder and bowel emptying reflexes are spinal; the brainstem handles heart rate, blood pressure and breathing.

questions.stem: Autonomic effects on the heart and vessels:
options: Most vessels have a rich parasympathetic innervation
Sympathetic: ↑ heart rate, via NE → β₁
Most vessels constrict through NE → α₁
Parasympathetic: ↓ heart rate, via ACh → Nn on the cardiac cells
questions.explanation: Parasympathetic slowing of the heart uses ACh → M₂ (Nn receptors are in the ganglia). Most blood vessels receive only sympathetic fibres: their tone is set by ↑ or ↓ sympathetic activity. Skeletal-muscle vessels dilate with circulating adrenaline (β₂).

questions.stem: Autonomic effects on the eye and bronchi:
options: Accommodation for near vision is sympathetic
Pupil constriction is parasympathetic: ACh → M₃ on the sphincter
Bronchodilation is due mainly to circulating adrenaline acting on β₂
Pupil dilation is sympathetic: NE → α₁ on the radial dilator muscle
questions.explanation: Near-vision accommodation is parasympathetic (ciliary muscle contraction, ACh → M₃); sympathetic β₂ causes slight ciliary relaxation for far vision.

questions.stem: About autonomic effects on the viscera:
options: Bladder storage: the detrusor relaxes (NE → β₃) and the internal sphincter contracts (NE → α₁)
Bladder emptying: the detrusor contracts through ACh → M₃
Parasympathetic activity increases insulin and enzyme secretion through M₃
Bladder storage is a parasympathetic effect
questions.explanation: Storage is sympathetic, emptying parasympathetic. In the pancreas, sympathetic NE → α₂ decreases insulin; parasympathetic ACh → M₃ increases it.

questions.stem: About salivary secretion:
options: Parasympathetic stimulation gives a scant, protein-rich secretion
Salivation is an example of opposing effects of the two divisions
Salivation is an example of complementary effects of the two divisions
Sympathetic stimulation gives an abundant watery secretion through ACh → M₃
questions.explanation: Parasympathetic: abundant watery secretion (ACh → M₃); sympathetic: scant, protein-rich secretion. Both stimulate secretion with different composition: complementary, not opposing, effects.

questions.stem: About sexual function and single innervation:
options: Most blood vessels, sweat glands, the adrenal medulla and the kidney receive only sympathetic fibres
Erection is parasympathetic, through vasodilation via NO
Gut motility is increased by sympathetic activity
Emission and ejaculation are sympathetic, through NE → α₁
questions.explanation: "Point and Shoot": parasympathetic = point (erection), sympathetic = shoot. The sympathetic system decreases gut motility; the parasympathetic increases it.
